name_en: Tofu — soybean curd, set from soy milk with nigari
summary_ja: 大豆を浸して砕き、煮て搾った豆乳を、にがりなどの凝固剤で固めた仕込み物。工程は全国ほぼ同じとされるが、水の抜き方や豆乳の濃さ、固めた後の扱いで木綿・絹ごし・堅豆腐・寄せ豆腐などに分かれ、土地ごとの型を持つという。
summary_en: Soybeans soaked, ground, simmered, and pressed into soy milk, then set with a coagulant such as nigari. The process is said to be nearly the same nationwide, yet how the water is drawn off, how rich the milk is, and what happens after setting split it into momen, kinugoshi, firm mountain tofu, and soft curds, each with a regional shape.

summary_ja: 豆乳をにがりで寄せ、布を敷いた穴あきの型箱に崩し入れて重しで水を抜いた豆腐。表面に布目が残り、しっかりした歯ごたえと濃い豆の味を持つとされる。煮物や炒め物、田楽や焼き豆腐のもとになる基本の型という。
summary_en: Soy milk curded with nigari, broken into a cloth-lined, perforated mold and weighted to press out water. The cloth leaves its weave on the surface, and the block is said to hold a firm bite and a concentrated bean flavor — the basic form behind simmered dishes, stir-fries, dengaku, and grilled tofu.

name_en: Kinugoshi-dofu — smooth silken tofu set whole in the mold
summary_ja: 濃いめの豆乳を型箱の中で凝固剤と合わせ、崩さず水も抜かずにそのまま固めた豆腐。絹のようになめらかな舌触りからこの名で呼ばれるとされ、冷奴や湯豆腐、汁物のように豆腐そのものの口当たりを味わう食べ方に向くという。
summary_en: Richer soy milk combined with coagulant inside the mold and set whole, never broken or pressed. Named for a texture said to be as smooth as silk, it suits dishes where tofu itself is the point — chilled hiyayakko, simmered yudofu, and soups.

name_ja: 寄せ豆腐（おぼろ豆腐・ざる豆腐）
name_en: Yose-dofu — soft curds scooped before pressing, also called oboro or zaru tofu
summary_ja: 豆乳ににがりを打って寄せた凝固物を、型に入れず桶やざるに掬ったままの豆腐。おぼろ豆腐、ざる豆腐とも呼ばれるとされ、水に晒さないため豆の甘みと香りが濃く、ふわりと崩れる食感が持ち味という。
summary_en: Curds formed by stirring nigari into soy milk and scooped straight into a tub or bamboo basket, never pressed in a mold. Also called oboro-dofu or zaru-dofu, it skips the cold-water soak, so the bean's sweetness and aroma stay concentrated and the texture collapses softly on the tongue.

name_en: Yaki-dofu — pressed tofu seared for simmering without crumbling
summary_ja: 水を切った木綿豆腐の表面を直火やバーナーであぶり、焼き目をつけた豆腐。表面が締まって煮崩れしにくく、だしや割り下を吸いやすいとされ、すき焼きや雑煮、煮物に欠かせない型という。
summary_en: Firm momen tofu, drained and seared over open flame or a burner until the surface is marked. The seared skin keeps it from breaking apart and lets it drink in broth or sukiyaki sauce, making it the standard tofu for sukiyaki, New Year's zoni, and simmered dishes.

name_ja: 五箇山豆腐（五箇山の堅豆腐）
name_en: Gokayama-dofu — the rope-tied firm tofu of Toyama's snowbound Gokayama valley
summary_ja: 富山県南砺市の五箇山地区に伝わる、縄で縛って持ち運べるほど硬い豆腐。濃い豆乳をにがりで固め、強く圧して水を抜くとされ、豪雪の合掌造り集落で保存と携行に適した形として受け継がれてきたという。報恩講の煮物に欠かせないとされる。
summary_en: A tofu from the Gokayama district of Nanto, Toyama, firm enough to carry tied with rope. Rich soy milk is set with nigari and pressed hard to drive out water, a shape said to have suited storage and transport in these heavy-snow villages of steep-roofed gassho houses. It is considered essential to the stews of the Hoonko memorial meal.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 報恩講料理（富山県）

name_en: Shiramine kata-dofu — hard mountain tofu of Hakusan's Shiramine village, Ishikawa
summary_ja: 石川県白山市白峰に伝わる、縄で縛って運べるほど硬い豆腐。濃い豆乳を固めて強く圧搾するとされ、夏の間山の小屋に住み込んで畑を耕す「出作り」の暮らしの携行食として受け継がれたという。薄く切って刺身のように食べる習わしも伝わる。
summary_en: A hard tofu from Shiramine, a village in the Hakusan foothills of Ishikawa, firm enough to carry tied with rope. Rich soy milk is set and pressed hard, and it is said to have been carried by families who spent summers farming from mountain huts, a practice called dezukuri. Slicing it thin and eating it like sashimi is also a local custom.

name_en: Shima-dofu — Okinawa's large, firm island tofu, sold warm from the press
summary_ja: 沖縄で作られる、大きく硬い豆腐。呉を煮る前に搾る生搾り法と、にがりに塩を加える仕込みが特徴とされ、一丁が本土の倍ほどの重さという。できたてを温かいまま「あちこーこー」で売る習慣が残り、チャンプルーなど炒め物に欠かせない食材とされる。
summary_en: Okinawa's large, firm tofu. It is made by the raw-press method — squeezing the soybean slurry before simmering — and often set with salt added to the nigari; a single block weighs about twice a mainland one. Shops still sell it warm straight from the press, a custom called achikoko, and it is the tofu that makes a chanpuru a chanpuru.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 ゴーヤーチャンプルー（沖縄県）

name_en: Yushi-dofu — Okinawa's soft, unpressed curds eaten with their liquid
summary_ja: 沖縄で、島豆腐に固める前の寄せた状態をそのまま汁ごと食べる豆腐。ふわふわと崩れる食感と豆乳の甘みが持ち味とされ、塩や醤油で味を調えて朝食の汁物にしたり、沖縄そばに載せたりするという。寄せ豆腐と同じ発想が島で独自に続いたものとされる。
summary_en: Okinawa's tofu eaten at the stage before it becomes shima-dofu: soft curds served in their own liquid. Fluffy, collapsing, and sweet with fresh soy milk, it is seasoned with salt or soy sauce as a breakfast soup or ladled over Okinawa soba. It is the island's own version of the mainland's yose-dofu idea, kept alive on its own terms.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 沖縄県

name_en: Iya iwa-dofu — the rock-hard tofu of Tokushima's Iya valley
summary_ja: 徳島県三好市の祖谷地方に伝わる、縄で縛って運べるほど硬い豆腐。石豆腐とも呼ばれ、濃い豆乳を固めて強く圧し、塩気をきかせて仕上げるとされる。急峻な山里で運搬と保存に向く形として受け継がれ、雑煮やでこまわしの具に欠かせないという。
summary_en: A tofu from the Iya valley in Miyoshi, Tokushima, hard enough to carry tied with rope and nicknamed 'stone tofu.' Rich soy milk is set, pressed hard, and finished on the salty side. It is said to have taken this form for carrying and keeping in a steep mountain district, and it is essential to the local New Year's zoni and to the skewered dekomawashi.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 うちがえ雑煮（徳島県）

name_en: Tsuto-dofu — tofu bound in a straw sheath and boiled, from Fukushima's Aizu
summary_ja: 木綿豆腐をわらで編んだ苞（つと）に包み、湯で煮て締めた豆腐。表面にわらの筋が残り、煮崩れしにくく保存がきくとされ、福島県の会津地方で冠婚葬祭の煮しめに使われてきたという。茨城県にも同じ名の豆腐が伝わる。
summary_en: Momen tofu wrapped in a woven straw sheath (tsuto) and boiled until it tightens. The straw leaves ridges on the surface, and the block is said to resist falling apart and keep longer, which made it the tofu for ceremonial nishime stews in Fukushima's Aizu region. Ibaraki has a tofu of the same name.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 つゆ煮しめ（福島県）

name_en: Juten-dofu — packaged silken tofu set inside its sealed container
summary_ja: 冷やした豆乳と凝固剤を容器に入れて密封し、湯の中で加熱して容器の中で固めた豆腐。水に晒さず空気に触れないため日持ちが長く、きめがなめらかで絹ごしに近いとされる。スーパーで水のない容器に入って並ぶ豆腐の多くがこの型という。
summary_en: Chilled soy milk and coagulant filled into a container, sealed, and heated in hot water so the tofu sets inside its own package. Never soaked in water or exposed to air, it keeps far longer than other tofu and has a smooth, kinugoshi-like grain. Most supermarket tofu sold in a waterless tray is this type.
